4º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 8

Places in town: there is / there are

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Learn the names of places in a town
  • Use there is with one thing and there are with more than one
  • Make negatives and questions: there isn't, Is there…?
  • Describe your town with prepositions of place
  • Talk about transport: by bus, on foot
  • Ask for and give directions in a town
  • Learn about London, a big city
  • Use there was and there were to compare a town in the past and now

Para pensar

En español decimos «hay un parque» y «hay dos parques», con la misma palabra. ¿Pasa lo mismo en inglés?

Explicación

1. Places in town

Let's learn the places in a town: school, park, library (biblioteca), hospital, supermarket, bakery (panadería), post office (correos), police station (comisaría), train station (estación de tren), cinema, museum, swimming pool, restaurant, café and bank.

Ojo con los falsos amigos: library no es «librería», es biblioteca. Una librería es un bookshop. Y pharmacy o chemist's es la farmacia.

2. Getting around: transport

How do you get to school? How do people travel in a town or a city? Here are the most common types of transport:

  • by bus (en autobús), by car, by taxi, by bike, by train, by underground / by metro, by tram, by plane, by boat.
  • But: on foot (a pie). We say «I go to school on foot» or «I walk to school».

Questions and answers:

  • «How do you get to school?» → «I go by bus.»
  • «How does your dad go to work?» → «He goes by train.»
  • «How long does it take?» (¿Cuánto tardas?) → «About fifteen minutes.»

Places for transport:

  • bus stop (parada de autobús)
  • train station (estación de tren)
  • underground station (estación de metro)
  • airport (aeropuerto)
  • car park (aparcamiento)
  • bike lane (carril bici)

Which transport is the best for the planet? Walking and cycling don't pollute at all! Buses, trams and trains are also good, because many people travel together. Cars and planes pollute the most.

Remember: by + transport, with no the: «by bus», not «by the bus».

3. There is: one thing

We use there is (short form: there's) to say that one thing exists in a place: «There's a park near my house», «There is a big tree in the square», «There's an old castle in my town».

After there is we usually put a or an. We also use it with things we can't count: «There's some water in the bottle». En castellano: there is = «hay» cuando hablamos de una sola cosa.

4. There are: more than one

We use there are for two or more things: «There are three schools in my town», «There are some shops in my street», «There are lots of trees in the park».

The noun goes in plural: schools, shops, trees. The short form there're exists, but it's not common in writing. Truco: mira lo que viene después. ¿Es una cosa? → is. ¿Son varias? → are. «There is a cinema. There are two cinemas.»

5. Negatives: there isn't, there aren't

To say that something doesn't exist, add not: there isn't (there is not) and there aren't (there are not). «There isn't a zoo in my town», «There aren't any mountains near Valladolid».

With there aren't we usually use any: «There aren't any museums». En castellano: «no hay» se dice there isn't para una cosa y there aren't any para varias. Fíjate: en las afirmativas usamos some, y en las negativas, any.

6. Questions: Is there…? Are there…?

For questions, we change the order: Is there a bank near here? Are there any parks in your town? The short answers are: «Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.» and «Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.»

To ask about numbers: «How many schools are there in your town?» – «There are two». En castellano: «¿Hay un banco cerca?» → «Is there a bank near here?». Es muy útil cuando estás de viaje y buscas algo.

7. Where is it? Prepositions of place

To say where places are, we use prepositions: next to (al lado de), opposite (enfrente de), between (entre), behind (detrás de), in front of (delante de), near (cerca de) and on the corner (en la esquina).

Examples: «The bakery is next to the bank», «The library is opposite the park», «The café is between the cinema and the school». Consejo: dibuja un mapa sencillo y practica con flechas; las preposiciones se aprenden mejor viéndolas.

8. Asking for and giving directions

When you are in a new town and you are lost (perdido), you need to ask for directions.

Asking:

  • «Excuse me, where is the station, please?»
  • «Excuse me, how do I get to the museum?»
  • «Is there a bank near here?»
  • «Is it far?» (¿Está lejos?)

Giving directions:

  • Go straight on (sigue recto).
  • Turn left (gira a la izquierda) / Turn right (gira a la derecha).
  • Take the first / second street on the left.
  • Go past the bank (pasa el banco).
  • Cross the road (cruza la calle).
  • It's on the corner (en la esquina).
  • It's on the left / on the right.
  • It's opposite the park (enfrente del parque).
  • It's between the café and the cinema.
  • It's next to the library.

Notice that we use the imperative to give directions: Go, Turn, Take, Cross.

And always finish politely: «Thank you very much!» → «You're welcome!» (¡De nada!)

9. Town or city?

A village (pueblo pequeño) is small: there are a few houses, a church and maybe a shop. A town is bigger: there are schools, shops, a market and a library. A city (ciudad) is very big: there are lots of buildings, an airport, big hospitals, museums and a lot of traffic.

Describing where you live: «I live in a village near Teruel. There's a small square and there are two cafés. There isn't a cinema, but there's a swimming pool in summer». Pregunta: ¿tú vives en un village, en un town o en una city?

10. London: a big city

London is the capital city of the United Kingdom and of England. About nine million people live there. It's one of the most visited cities in the world. What is there in London?

  • The River Thames (el río Támesis) goes through the city. There are lots of bridges. The most famous is Tower Bridge: it opens in the middle to let big boats pass!
  • Big Ben is the famous bell in the clock tower of the Houses of Parliament.
  • Buckingham Palace is where the King lives when he's in London. You can watch the Changing of the Guard, with soldiers in red jackets and tall black hats.
  • The London Eye is a giant wheel next to the river. From the top, you can see the whole city.
  • There are fantastic museums, like the Natural History Museum and the British Museum. Many of them are free!
  • There are big parks, like Hyde Park.

To travel around London, people take the red double-decker buses (autobuses de dos pisos), the black taxis called cabs, or the Underground, which Londoners call the Tube. It's the oldest underground railway in the world!

Would you like to visit London? What would you like to see first?

11. Reading: welcome to Riverton

Read Ella's text: «I live in Riverton, a small town near the sea. There's a beautiful beach and there are lots of fish restaurants. In the centre there's a square with a fountain. The library is opposite the town hall. There are two schools and a sports centre. There isn't a cinema, but there's a theatre next to the market. There aren't any tall buildings. I love my town!»

Answer: Is there a cinema in Riverton? Where is the library? How many schools are there?

12. Let's practise: design your dream town

Draw a map of your dream town (pueblo ideal). Add at least eight places: maybe a chocolate factory, a skate park or a giant library! Then write a description: «In my dream town there is a big water park. There are three ice cream shops. The zoo is next to the castle. There isn't any traffic: people go by bike».

Swap maps with a partner and ask questions: «Is there a football stadium?», «How many parks are there?». Consejo: comprueba que usas is con una cosa y are con varias.

13. There was, there were: my town in the past

To talk about a place in the past, we use there was (singular) and there were (plural). It's like there is / there are, but in the past:

  • «There was a cinema in my street.» (Había un cine.)
  • «There were lots of farms near the town.» (Había muchas granjas.)

Negative: there wasn't, there weren't.

  • «There wasn't a supermarket.» «There weren't any traffic lights.»

Questions: Was there…? Were there…?

  • «Was there a school?» → «Yes, there was.» / «No, there wasn't.»
  • «Were there any cars?» → «Yes, there were, but not many.»

Read how Grandpa Luis describes his town seventy years ago:

When I was a boy, my town was very small. There was one school, one church and one little shop. There were lots of fields around the town and there were many horses and donkeys. There weren't many cars. There wasn't a swimming pool, so we swam in the river!

Now compare: «Now there is a big sports centre. There are three schools.»

Ask an older person in your family: what was your town like in the past?

14. A poster about your town

Let's make a poster in English to show visitors the best things in your town or city! Follow these steps:

  1. Title: «Welcome to…!» or «Visit…!»
  2. Introduction: where is your town? How big is it? «Calatayud is a town in Aragón, in the north-east of Spain. About twenty thousand people live there.»
  3. Places to visit: use there is / there are. «There is a beautiful old castle on a hill. There are lots of churches and a long river.»
  4. Things to do: use you can. «You can walk along the river. You can eat delicious food in the restaurants.»
  5. How to get there: «You can go by train or by bus from Zaragoza.»
  6. A final sentence: «Come and visit us!»

Tips for a great poster:

  • Add photos or drawings with short labels.
  • Use big letters for the title.
  • Include a simple map with the most important places.
  • Check your spelling and capital letters (names of places always start with a capital letter).

When the posters are ready, the class can make a tourist exhibition!

There is / there are

Ejercicios

  1. Translate: biblioteca, panadería, comisaría, estación de tren.

  2. Complete with is or are: «There ___ a cinema.»

  3. Complete with is or are: «There ___ five parks.»

  4. Make it negative: «There is a museum.»

  5. Make a question: «There are some cafés.»

  6. Short answer (yes): «Is there a bank near here?»

  7. Translate: «La farmacia está enfrente del colegio.»

  8. What's the difference between a village and a city?

  9. Correct: «In my street have two shops.»

  10. Write three sentences about your town.

  11. Complete: I go to school ___ bus.

  12. How do you say «sigue recto»?

  13. What is the Tube?

  14. Complete: ___ was a castle.

  15. Answer to «Thank you very much!»

  16. Complete: ___ there any shops? Yes, there were.

  17. Write a question to ask where the station is.

  18. Name three famous places in London.

  19. How do you get to school? Answer.

  20. Correct: There weren't a supermarket.

  21. Give directions from your school to your house.

  22. Make a poster about your town.

  23. Compare your town in the past and now.

  24. Plan a day in London: what would you visit?

Practica

  1. «Hay un parque» is…

    1. A) There are a park.
    2. B) It has a park.
    3. C) There is a park.

  2. «There ___ three schools.»

    1. A) are
    2. B) is
    3. C) be

  3. «Library» means…

    1. A) librería
    2. B) biblioteca
    3. C) laboratorio

  4. «There aren't ___ museums.»

    1. A) some
    2. B) any
    3. C) a

  5. Which question is correct?

    1. A) There is a bakery?
    2. B) Are there a bakery?
    3. C) Is there a bakery?

  6. Short answer: «Are there any parks?» (no)

    1. A) No, there aren't.
    2. B) No, there isn't.
    3. C) No, they aren't.

  7. «Opposite» means…

    1. A) al lado de
    2. B) detrás de
    3. C) enfrente de

  8. «Between» means…

    1. A) cerca
    2. B) entre
    3. C) encima

  9. «How many cinemas ___ there?»

    1. A) are
    2. B) is
    3. C) do

  10. A very big town with an airport is a…

    1. A) city
    2. B) village
    3. C) square

  11. I walk to school = I go to school…

    1. A) by foot
    2. B) on foot
    3. C) by walk

  12. «Gira a la izquierda» is…

    1. A) Turn right
    2. B) Go straight on
    3. C) Turn left

  13. The famous bell in London is…

    1. A) Tower Bridge
    2. B) Big Ben
    3. C) the Tube

  14. ___ were lots of horses.

    1. A) There
    2. B) It
    3. C) They

  15. Was there a pool? No, there ___ .

    1. A) weren't
    2. B) isn't
    3. C) wasn't

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Los lugares de un pueblo o ciudad en inglés; Cuándo se usa there is y cuándo there are; Cómo se hacen negativas y preguntas con there; Las preposiciones para decir dónde está un lugar.

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

there isHay (una cosa).
there areHay (varias cosas).
there isn'tNo hay (una).
there aren't anyNo hay (ninguno).
Is there…?¿Hay…? (una).
libraryBiblioteca (no librería).
next toAl lado de.
oppositeEnfrente de.
Transportby bus, by train, by bike; on foot.
DirectionsGo straight on, turn left, it's opposite the park.
LondonBig Ben, Tower Bridge, London Eye, the Tube.
There was / wereThere was a cinema. There were horses.

Soluciones

  1. C) Uno: there is.
  2. A) Plural.
  3. B) Falso amigo.
  4. B) Negativa: any.
  5. C) Is there…?
  6. A) Plural.
  7. C) opposite.
  8. B) between.
  9. A) How many + are.
  10. A) city.
  11. B) Transport.
  12. C) Directions.
  13. B) London.
  14. A) There was / were.
  15. C) There was / were.

  2. is.
  3. are.
  4. There isn't a museum.
  5. Are there any cafés?
  6. Yes, there is.
  7. The chemist's (pharmacy) is opposite the school.
  8. A village is very small; a city is very big.
  9. In my street there are two shops.
  10. Model answer: There is a big park. There are two supermarkets. There isn't a zoo.
  11. by
  12. Go straight on.
